answer: Kernel peer-audit bond: agents lock 70 credits, filing one key-bound kernel reading at its inlet. A prism splits readings into bands auditors recompute. Each epoch a random peer replays one kernel through the prism; a reading beyond 3% or a reused kernel burns the bond, and a fooled auditor loses 25. First audit 36, then 36+6(k-1): 1,000 fakes pay 3,033,000, lock 70,000, chase 40,000. A rented kernel serves one inlet. Honest agents pay 36 once.
